proposal.root_problem: Dispute ticket volume roughly doubled from ~600/month (Jun-Jul 2026) to ~1180-1260/month (Aug-Sep 2026) (E-05). The best-supported mechanism (H-RULE-CHANGE, H-HIGH-CONSUMPTION-REJECT) is that billing-import validation rule BV-17, deployed 2026-08-01 (E-12), rejects valid AMI meter reads flagged as high-consumption at import even when received and exported before cutoff: 1184 of the 1240 disputed ESTIMATED-read bills (95.5%) show exactly this REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION pattern (E-11), forcing estimate substitution and producing bills customers dispute as wrong.

symptoms: Dispute ticket volume roughly doubled from ~600/month in Jun/Jul 2026 to ~1180-1260/month in Aug/Sep 2026 (E-05).

1240 of 3025 disputed bills carry read_type ESTIMATED (E-01); of these, 1184 (95.5%) had a valid AMI read received before cutoff and exported to billing but rejected at import with status REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION (E-11).

Billing-config validation rule BV-17, a high-consumption check comparing raw register value to 12-month m3 history with unit_scaling 'none', was deployed 2026-08-01, matching the dispute-surge onset (E-12).

Meter firmware v4.2 (rolled out 2026-06) reports register readings in 0.1 m3 units while firmware v3.x reports directly in m3 (E-13), a candidate explanation for spurious high-consumption rejections under BV-17's unscaled comparison.
causal_chain: Billing import validation rule BV-17 (high-consumption check comparing raw register value against 12-month m3 history, unit_scaling: none) was deployed 2026-08-01 (E-12), coinciding with the onset of the dispute surge.

At billing import, AMI reads flagged by BV-17 as high-consumption are rejected even when received before cutoff and already exported to billing: 1184 of 1240 disputed ESTIMATED-read bills (95.5%) show this REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION pattern (E-11).
Rejected reads trigger estimate substitution instead of the actual meter read, producing bills with read_type ESTIMATED among the disputed population (E-01, F-11).

Customers receiving these rejected-read/estimate-substituted bills, and potentially the 1785 ACTUAL-read disputed bills affected by the same BV-17 check (E-01), perceive incorrect billing and file dispute tickets.
Monthly dispute ticket volume rises from a ~600/month baseline (Jun/Jul 2026) to ~1180-1260/month (Aug/Sep 2026), roughly doubling (E-05).

The 56 NO_READ_RECEIVED cases (4.5% of the 1240 ESTIMATED-read disputes, E-11) are assumed to be a minor residual unrelated to the dominant BV-17 mechanism rather than a sign of a separate unresolved field/AMI delivery gap.

proposal.summary: The problem (PD-1, v2): billing-dispute tickets roughly doubled from ~600/month in Jun-Jul 2026 to ~1180-1260/month in Aug-Sep 2026 (E-05). The best-supported cause is billing-import rule BV-17, deployed 2026-08-01, which rejects valid AMI reads flagged as high-consumption even when received before cutoff (E-11, E-12), forcing estimate substitution and wrong bills. The release delivers an escalation memo (W-ESCALATE) to Billing Operations (SH-BILL) recommending BV-17 correction, with no automated bill writes or route changes. Decision: RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION. The DEFINE gate was only CONDITIONAL_PASS, and a Layer-1 semantic check found the memo's wording calls the unit-scaling mechanism 'confirmed' while the obligation to verify it is still OPEN - the harness released anyway, disclosing this and other open items as limitations rather than holding.
key_points: Requester SH-CS originally framed this as a response-speed problem needing an auto-fix agent (CL-01, H-RESPONSE-SPEED); this was rejected since ticket response is within SLA (E-04).

An earlier problem framing (PD-1@v1) assumed two parallel causes - a rule change for ACTUAL-read bills plus a staffing/route-gap cause for ESTIMATED-read bills (E-03, E-06) - but was invalidated when E-11 showed 95.5% of ESTIMATED-read disputes are the same import-rejection mechanism, leading to rejection of H-AMI-GAP, H-FIELD-READ-GAP and H-STAFFING-SHORTAGE.

Billing-config confirms BV-17 (unit_scaling 'none') deployed 2026-08-01 matching the surge onset (E-12); firmware v4.2 reports in 0.1 m3 units vs v3.x in m3 (E-13), suggesting a plausible unit-mismatch cause, but a direct attempt to fetch raw register values (E-16) returned no such data, so H-UNIT-SCALING-BUG remains CANDIDATE, not confirmed.

The deliverable is the escalation memo (W-ESCALATE) to SH-BILL within authorized scope (escalate_rule_correction:SH-BILL); no write_bill_adjustment or push_route_update is included, respecting K-BILLWRITE and K-DISPATCH.
